title: Order cancellation and refunds
intro: Agree on cancellation scope, order-value recalculation, and refund behavior before implementation.
coverage_note: An illustrative example with hypothetical data. For a real project, the agent should inspect the specification and code, then replace these questions with project-specific ones.

questions.title: What cancellation scope should customers have?
questions.context: An order can contain multiple items. This answer determines which follow-up rules apply.

options.label: Customers cannot cancel orders themselves
options.detail: Employees handle cancellations outside the scope of this investigation.

options.label: Cancel the entire order or individual items

questions.title: Can a paid order be cancelled?
Which order statuses remain eligible for cancellation?
questions.why: Select every applicable status. If another status applies, choose Other and describe it.

questions.title: How should the discount change after a partial cancellation?
questions.context: Example: a 600,000 VND order receives a 50,000 VND discount after meeting the 500,000 VND threshold. After one item is cancelled, the remaining items have a list price of only 400,000 VND.

options.label: Recalculate the discount based on the remaining items
Block partial cancellation if the remaining items no longer qualify for the discount

questions.why: Partial cancellation raises a decision about voucher eligibility. Resolve this rule before calculating the refund amount.

questions.title: How should shipping fees be handled for partial cancellation?

options.label: Keep the order's shipping fee unchanged
Recalculate based on the remaining items

questions.context: If the rule depends on delivery timing or who pays the fee, describe it in the notes.

questions.title: After a cancellation is approved, how soon should the refund be issued?
questions.context: Enter the maximum number of days. Use 0 for a same-day refund; specify calendar or business days in the notes.

questions.title: How can each role request and approve a cancellation?
questions.context: Add one row for each role. Enter its rules in the same row so roles and their count do not need to be predicted in advance.

questions.title: Is a “Refund processing” status acceptable?
questions.context: The system has accepted the request but has not received a result from the payment provider. This is a user-experience decision.

options.label: Yes; show the status and update it when the result arrives
No; agree on a different behavior before implementation

questions.title: If an order has shipped, what conditions determine whether cancellation is accepted?
questions.context: Describe who confirms the return, who pays any fees, and when the case moves to the returns process.

questions.title: Does the payment provider currently support multiple refunds for one transaction?
questions.context: This example does not include provider documentation for the agent to verify. DEV should check the contract/API and record the source in the notes; choose Undecided if the information is unavailable.

questions.title: How will the refund flow return its result?

options.label: Accept the request, process it in the background, then update the status

questions.context: Check the integration capability against the behavior BA requested in S08.

questions.title: How will duplicate refunds be prevented and failures recovered?
questions.context: Describe the idempotency key, persisted state, retry behavior, and reconciliation process.

questions.title: What data changes are needed to represent cancelled items and allocated amounts?
questions.context: Assumed example behavior: payments are recorded for the whole order. Use the BA's selected rules to propose a representation and check consistency.

constraints.message: BA rejected a pending status, but DEV chose background processing. Align on the expected behavior before implementation.

scout_log.hypothesis: If individual items can be cancelled
scout_log.finding: Threshold-based vouchers and order-level fees create additional decisions

coverage.stop_reason: The example's key decisions are represented
Questions about discounts, fees, and allocation have been added

open_items.description: Hypothetical example; inspect real sources before applying this to a project
open_items.impact: Do not treat example answers as project decisions
